newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo improving in most areas-Gyll.
newsitem.headline: Volvo improving in most areas-Gyll.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo is on the road to improvement in virtually every area of the group, chief executive Soren Gyll said on Wednesday.
"We are heading towards a clear improvement in practically every area," Gyll told a news conference. "To date we have fulfilled three of the goals in the programme we set up in 1995.
"We have focused on core business operations -- the divestment process is almost completed; we have full control of the strategic business operation; we have a strong balance sheet," Gyll said.
But Gyll said the market situation was still not good for the company that on Wednesday posted a 12 percent drop in sales in the first nine months of 1996 to 113.6 billion crowns.
Truck sales fell 14 percent with continuing weak demand in North and South America and car sales fell five percent.
"The situation for trucks is today not satisfactory, even if it is good in Europe," Gyll said.
"For cars the trend in results is positive even though it is still at a low level. We are continuing to follow our plans from 1994 and will increase steps to fulfill these."
To do this Volvo will increase productivity and improve cost efficiency, Gyll said.
Volvo's finance director Jan Engstrom pointed out that Volvo's operating margins were still a long way from the company's aim of five to seven percent.
"The third quarter (of 1996) the operating margin was two percent, a long way from the 5.3 percent in 1995," Engstrom said.
"We must have better operating profits; here we have a problem. The company is ready but profits must rise," said Engstrom.
